content:
## Source
.design/m5/43-federation.md — REQ-1, REQ-5, AC-1, AC-4 + decomposition PR 3.

## Surface
- New file: `polaris-backend/src/federation/publish.rs` — wraps the existing repo-write path to publish escalation records to the operator's ATProto repo.
- New file: `polaris-backend/src/bin/polaris_federation_escalate.rs` (or extend an existing admin bin) — `polaris federation-escalate --incident <id> --to <did>` admin command.
- Extend `polaris-types::lexicon_mapping` (lands in #103 from NSIDs epic) with the `Escalation` → `polaris_lexicons::Escalation` mapping. The privacy boundary lives in this mapping function.

## Mapping privacy boundary (REQ-5)
The mapping function strips:
- `moderator_id` → replaced with instance DID
- Internal audit-chain hash → omitted entirely
- Reporter DIDs from referenced incidents → omitted
- Exposure-tracking metadata → omitted

Each drop annotated in source: `// privacy: <field> never federated`.

## Rust-quality notes
- **Use existing repo-write path.** v1 has `polaris-publish-labeler-record` (in-repo binary) and `proto_blue_xrpc::client::*` repo write primitives. Reuse, don't reinvent.
- **The mapping function is the privacy boundary, not the publish function.** Per the architect pattern of "one place to enforce a rule": `to_lexicon_escalation()` strips internal-only fields; `publish_escalation()` only handles transport. If the publish layer ever needs to strip something, that's a design smell — push it back into the mapping function.
- **Unit-test the privacy boundary**: take a sample `polaris_types::EscalationMessage` with a moderator ID; map to wire form; `assert!(serde_json::to_string(&wire).unwrap().find("moderator_id").is_none())`. Same test for audit-chain hash, reporter DID, exposure metadata.
- **Repo writes are signed by the labeler key.** Use the existing `ApiState::active_signer` watch channel (introduced in v1 issue #65 rotation work) — the same signer that signs labels signs federation records.
- **`#[must_use]` on every public publish function** — a forgotten `?` on a publish call would silently drop a federation escalation.
- The admin binary's CLI uses `clap` (already a workspace dep). Pattern: `#[derive(clap::Parser)]` on a `FederationEscalateArgs` struct.

## External references
- proto-blue repo write client: `/home/doll/proto-blue/proto-blue/proto-blue-xrpc/src/client.rs`
- v1 label emit (signed repo-record reference): `polaris-backend/src/labeler/emitter.rs`
- v1 `active_signer` watch channel: `polaris-backend/src/api/state.rs`
- clap derive: https://docs.rs/clap/latest/clap/_derive/index.html

## Acceptance (AC-1, AC-4)
- [ ] AC-1: `polaris federation-escalate --incident <id> --to did:plc:test_target` writes a `polaris.escalation` record to the operator's repo. Within 10s, the target instance materializes it (verified by the PR 6 two-instance fixture).
- [ ] AC-4: Privacy boundary unit test asserts moderator_id, audit_chain_hash, reporter DIDs, and exposure metadata are absent from the serialized wire form. Run on every PR.
